name: Someone's Got You
description: Everyone shares a small goal; a classmate writes back one line of encouragement. Teacher approves every line.
when: When the class needs a kind word from each other, and you want to read every line first.

notes: I want to speak up at least once in science this week.
I am learning a hard song on guitar and my fingers hurt.
Trying to get more sleep instead of scrolling until midnight.
I have a math test Friday and I am behind on the practice.
I finally started the art project I kept putting off.
Working on not saying sorry for everything.
Tryouts are next week and I am nervous.
I am trying to read a whole book this month, not just the first chapter.

lines: Your questions help the rest of us understand too. Ask the first one and the room gets easier.
Getting one tricky part right still counts as progress. Sore fingers mean you are actually doing it.
Choosing sleep over the scroll is hard. One early night this week is a real win.
Behind is not the same as lost. Two practice problems a night and Friday looks different.
Starting was the hardest part, and you already did it.
You do not owe anyone an apology for taking up space. Keep going.
Nervous means you care. Show up and do the thing you have practiced.
Chapter two is waiting. Ten pages tonight and you are past the part where most people stop.

intro.message:
SOMEONE'S GOT YOU

No points, no winners. You'll write one small real thing, then a classmate you don't get to pick writes something FOR you.

Write one kind, specific sentence. Small encouragement counts.

notes.prompt: One thing you're working on, wrestling with, or quietly proud of this week. Small is fine. 'trying to get more sleep' counts. One sentence.

boost.prompt:
A classmate wrote:

“{{notes.assigned}}”

Write them ONE kind, specific sentence. Talk to the thing they actually said: a skill they're learning, a project they're finishing, something new they're trying.

(Stuck? “Someone in this room is rooting for you” always counts.)

check.template: Read every line below before the wall goes up. Hide anything that isn't kind. When it's clean, open the wall.

foryou.content: Everyone is reading the line a classmate wrote for them. Give it a quiet minute, then open the wall.

wall.discussionPrompt: What did the good lines have in common? What makes encouragement land instead of bounce off?
wall.message: The encouragement wall, one line at a time.

end.message: That's a wrap. Look out for each other out there.
